To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CYP2A2, Cyp2B6, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, CYP1A1 and CYP3A2 SNPs, and genetic variation in the CYP2B and UGT2b7 3′- UTR are not associated with EFV plasma concentration, and that CYP2C8 and UGT2A1 SNPs, and the CYP2A1 3′-Utr SNP are associated
CYP2b6 c.516 and c.983 SNPs are important predictors of EFVs plasma concentrations after taking into account other SNPs, 3′- UTR genetic variation, and variables affecting metabolism of EFV.
the c.516G > T and c.983C > T polymorphisms of the cytochrome P450 2B6 gene were associated with efavirenz plasma concentrations in a South African population.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of pharmacogenetics determinates of EFV response among Black South African HAART recipients and the role of the 3′ untranslated region (UTR) in regulating drug metabolism and transport.
understanding the role of 3′- UTR SNPs in the context of the whole gene, and not as a single SNP.
the identification and evaluation of genetic determinants of inter-individual variability of EFV plasma levels and their potential role in the development of drug toxicity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CYP2B c.983T>G SNP is the strongest predictor of EFV plasma levels in this cohort, followed by CYP2B 516G>T.
CYP2A, CYP2C, CYP3, and UGTs are not major determinants of EFVs pharmacokinetic variability in Bantu-speaking South Africans.
the c.516G> T and c.983 T>C SNPs in Cyp2B6 are the most important determinants of efavirenz pharmacokinetics in black South Africans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CYP2A and CYP3A are the most important determinants of inter-individual variability of EFV plasma levels.
CYP2A, CYP3, and CYP4 gene variants do not play a major role in the pharmacokinetics of EFV.
the 3′ UTR SNPs do not have a significant effect on EFV pharmacokinetics, but that the 3’ UTR is a site of regulation of gene transcription and expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CYP2A, CYP2C, CYP1A, and UGT genes are not the major predictors of EFV pharmacokinetics in Bantu-speaking South Africans.
the 3′UTR is not a major determinant of EFV plasma levels.
CYP2A2 c.734G>A (rs28371655) is a significant predictor of EFV plasma levels.
